newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters won't state preferred partner.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters won't state preferred partner.

text.p: New Zealand First Party leader Winston Peters, who holds the balance of power, said on Tuesday he would not state his preferred coalition partner until he had reached a deal with either the caretaker National Party conservative government or centre-left Labour.
"We won't be stating it (a preference) before the deal is done," Peters said.
Peters also told a news conference that while he was working towards a coalition, he could not rule out the emergence of a minority National or Labour government.
He said he would do his utmost to reach a deal before parliament reconvenes on December 13. "All we can do is give it our best shot, and we are," he said.

Nationalist New Zealand First holds the balance of power after the October 12 election and is negotiating with both the caretaker National Party conservative government and centre-left Labour on coalition possibilities.
